Decision — Preferences on the COSMIC settings model

Status: accepted 2026-10-31. Amends desktop theming and style.

Context

A MixOS machine can run several desktops side by side, each on its own console: a distribution's own desktop (for example KWin and Plasma), a COSMIC session, and MixOS's own compositor (compd) with its shell (Quoin). MixOS egui applications already follow the settings authority, settingsd, on every desk. The desktops around them did not: each kept its own settings and its own look.

Preferences had grown layouts a person could not navigate: it was hard to tell which control changed which part of the screen.

COSMIC Settings (GPL-3.0) was studied clean-room as the model. Three findings decided the shape:

  • Only the settings app derives COSMIC's theme. It builds the full theme from a few inputs (mode, accent, tints, roundness, density, frosted glass, contrast); applications and the compositor read only the derived values.
  • COSMIC's own export to GTK and Qt is off by default.
  • Its page tree (about 45 pages and 190 controls, each control writing one key) maps cleanly onto one key prefix per page.

The decision

  1. settingsd is the one authority on a machine, for every desktop. Every setting COSMIC Settings offers becomes a settingsd key. One Preferences page is one key prefix.
    • Every setting has one value for every desktop. A value that is inherently per output (display layout, panel output, wallpaper per screen) is keyed by connector name, never per desktop.
    • Settings that a host service applies (displays, time, power, default applications) are still settingsd keys; the service follows them.
    • Live host state is not a setting. Hostname, users, firmware, network and Bluetooth inventories, battery and the About page are read and written live through hostd. Preferences shows and edits them; settingsd never stores them.
    • Each desktop's settingsd either is the authority or mirrors it. A mirror republishes the authority's revisions locally and forwards writes to it.
    • backdrop's wallpaper configuration moves into settingsd (wallpaper.*); backdrop becomes a follower.
  2. The key space changes in one clean break. A migration writes a new sealed record at the next store format and keeps the previous record beside it; settingsd downgrade converts back. There are no compatibility shims. The density float becomes three named steps, compact | comfortable | spacious.
  3. One theme derivation, one implementation. The derivation of the full palette, radii and spacing from the appearance inputs lives in libs/design. Every follower uses it: the toolkit (every egui application), compd's window decorations and Quoin. Exporters derive nothing: settingsd answers settings.palette with each mode's finished values, and the exporters write what they are given.
  4. Export to other desktops is one-way, by Mix Bus citizens. Each exporter follows settings revisions (no polling), owns the files it writes (one owner per file per desktop), reconciles once at start, and keeps the previous values for undo. Nothing is read back.
    • COSMIC: the theme inputs and derived theme for both modes, plus panel, dock, wallpaper, compositor and toolkit keys. COSMIC's own exporter is always switched off.
    • KDE Plasma: a colour scheme from the palette, fonts, accent and window decoration, then a reconfigure request. Plasma's panel configuration is snapshotted before any panel change, because its scripting interface has no undo.
    • GTK, Qt and the settings portal: on desktops that are not Plasma, GTK colour CSS and settings, qt5ct/qt6ct palettes, and the portal's colour scheme, accent and contrast. On Plasma these belong to Plasma's own bridges, which read the colour scheme the KDE exporter writes.
    • XDG: mimeapps.list and the autostart directory are rewritten from the default and startup application settings; Preferences is the way to change them.
    • appearance.export_toolkits gates the GTK, Qt and portal writes, and appearance.export_desktop gates the COSMIC and KDE exporters.
  5. Preferences is rebuilt in the shape of COSMIC Settings.
    • The same pages, order, page anatomy and controls. Values apply instantly; only display changes confirm, with a revert countdown.
    • The application and its command stay prefs; the window title is "Preferences".
    • A page or control whose backend does not exist yet is shown disabled, naming the missing backend, never hidden.
    • The sidebar card, the section card and the setting row are toolkit widgets that any application may use. Preferences gets no private chrome, and the title bar stays MixOS's own.
    • Every page and control is a Bus command: prefs.page.open navigates and prefs.ui.* operates controls as a person would. Values are still written only through settings.apply.
    • The old layouts are deleted.
  6. Where Preferences differs from COSMIC on purpose: search indexes every visible label and highlights the matched row; every control works from the keyboard; Escape closes a dialog. Everything else follows COSMIC, including "back" going to a page's parent.
  7. compd honours the window.* group: the gap between tiles (default 0), the active window hint, title-bar controls, clipping and tiled shadows.
  8. Missing backends are work items of their owners: input devices, workspaces, blur and accessibility features in compd; Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, time, locale, accounts, firmware and power in hostd; display changes in monitord; a new audio service over PipeWire; a daytime source for automatic light and dark; a screen reader and an on-screen keyboard. New services start as Mix Bus citizens unless Mix cannot do the job.
  9. Clean room. COSMIC (GPL-3.0 and MPL-2.0) is reference only. One reader studied the pinned source and wrote behaviour specifications; implementers receive the specifications without source references and never the source. MixOS takes no libcosmic dependency. Observing the running application is clean evidence.

Amendments to desktop theming and style

  • Mode auto: a daytime source resolves it to dark or light; followers never see auto.
  • Accent is an axis: auto, a named swatch (resolved per mode), or #rrggbb.
  • Derived schemes: a scheme may be authored as a few seed colours, from which libs/design derives every role. The default MixOS scheme becomes a derived one. Authored schemes stay.
  • Roundness: round | slightly_round | square overlays the style's radii and adds a pill radius.
  • Density: three named steps replace the float. Each keeps today's length multiplier and adds a spacing table for new surfaces. ui.reduced_motion and ui.text_scale move to accessibility.*.
  • Window and frosted groups: window.* (active hint, gap, title-bar controls, clipping, tiled shadows) and appearance.frosted.*.
  • Export keys: appearance.icon_theme, appearance.export_toolkits, appearance.export_desktop.
  • Placement: the advanced, registry-driven appearance controls move to Appearance › Experimental; per-application look lives under Applications › <application> › Look.

Consequences

  • One change in Preferences restyles the egui applications, the compositor, the shell, COSMIC, Plasma and GTK/Qt applications on every desktop of the machine.
  • Exporters write other desktops' configuration, so every export is undoable, and hand edits to files an exporter owns do not survive.
  • The settings and derivation work comes first, and the Preferences rebuild follows it.
  • Many controls wait on backends. Preferences ships with those controls disabled, and each backend lands on its own schedule.
